findings.claim: The new test asserts the Authorization header is forwarded on every page, but the test double (fetchMock) does not model the real upstream's rejection of a missing JWT, so the test cannot verify the fail-closed behavior the ticket cites.
findings.evidence: Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1645-the-audit-export-pages-its-rows-and-claims-no-type-filter.test.ts:35 `function upstream(url: string): Response {` and line 43 `return { ok: true, status: 200, json: async () => ({ success: true, data: { logs: f.slice(offset, offset + limit), total: f.length, limit, offset } }) } as unknown as Response;`
findings.test_or_reason: The test only checks that the header is present on each call; it does not check that the upstream would reject a call without it, so the test pins forwarding but not the fail-closed consequence.

findings.claim: The test only pins the 'Bearer' form of the Authorization header)Skip, not other forms, and only three pages, as the PR description itself acknowledges.
findings.evidence: PR DESCRIPTION: 'It pins three pages only, not more, and the `Bearer` form only, not other forms of the header.'
findings.test_or_reason: The PR description explicitly limits the scope; this is a limitation, not a defect.

findings.claim: The test's assertion on the Authorization header is not verified against the real route's header construction; it only checks the mocked fetch calls, so it does not prove the route sends the header in production.
findings.evidence: Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1645-the-audit-export-pages-its-rows-and-claims-no-type-filter.test.ts:194 `const sent = fetchMock.mock.calls.map((call) => ((call as unknown[])[1] as { headers?: Record<string, string> } | undefined)?.headers?.Authorization);`
findings.test_or_reason: The test inspects the mock's recorded calls, not the actual HTTP request the route would make; the mock is a stand-in for the real fetch, so the test pins the route's behavior only insofar as the mock faithfully represents it.
